senses.sense_definition: To give or leave personal property to someone by a last will and testament.

examples.text: In his will, he decided to <w>bequeath</w> his entire estate and art collection to the local museum.
She chose to <w>bequeath</w> a substantial sum of money to her favorite animal charity.

senses.sense_definition: To pass something down to future generations; to transmit.

examples.text: The previous generation had hoped to <w>bequeath</w> a cleaner and safer world to their children.
Ancient civilizations continue to <w>bequeath</w> rich cultural traditions and architectural wonders to modern society.

senses.sense_definition: To bestow, offer, or grant something as a gift or right.

examples.text: They refused to wait patiently for authorities to <w>bequeath</w> equal rights to ordinary citizens.
The ruler could arbitrarily <w>bequeath</w> titles and privileges upon favored courtiers.
